title: DataTap Jira: send the permission message now?

payload.prompt: Chris: do you send the Jira permission message to DataTap now, before you approve the Jira access card?
payload.detailsMarkdown:
## What you need to know

Nothing is connected to DataTap. Nothing is written to their Jira.

The Jira access card is in your queue. It is not approved. If you approve that card first, DataTap gives us a general Atlassian write grant on their production site. DataTap then learns how wide that grant is only after it granted the access.

The CTO decision expires on 7 October 2026. That date is not the deadline. Your approval of the access card is the deadline.

This message promises nothing. It tells DataTap that we write nothing. So it stays correct whichever way the CTO decides. Send it now or hold it. Either way you must know the fact below.

## The fact that changed the wording

The first draft told DataTap the grant can delete their tickets. **That is false.** Atlassian puts permanent delete in a separate permission group. That group is off by default. Only a DataTap admin can turn it on.

So the correct message is the good message: if their admin leaves it off, this grant cannot delete anything on their site.

## The message to send

Send it in the chat thread. Send it also by email. Their Atlassian admin does the work we ask for. That person may not be in the chat.

The greeting carries no name. The DataTap contact is on record only as "Client".

```
**Subject: before we connect Jira — what the connection can do**

Hi,

Before we connect Jira I wanted you to see what we found, rather than after.

The connection is an OAuth link to Atlassian's hosted connector. Atlassian documents that kind of connection as a general write grant, so I checked what that actually means for you:

- It stays on your Atlassian site, `codineasy.atlassian.net`. It cannot reach another site.
- **It is not limited to one project.** It reaches everything the authorising account can reach, and
Atlassian offers no way to narrow it to a single project. So I am not going to tell you we can do that.
- **It is not limited to comments.** On Jira, adding a comment is 1 of the 15 write actions
Atlassian lists — the rest cover creating and editing tickets, moving them through statuses, sprints and links, and attachments. There is no "comments only" version of this grant to ask for.
- The same connection also carries write access to Confluence and Bitbucket. That includes making a
private Confluence page publicly readable or granting other people access to it, and merging a pull request.

One piece of good news. **Permanent delete is not in that set.** Atlassian keeps delete and project-admin actions in separate permissions that are off by default and that only an admin can turn on. So unless your Atlassian admin enables them, this connection cannot delete anything on your site.

Two things would help, and both are before we connect rather than after:

1. Please leave those two permissions off, and tell me if your policy would force them on.
2. Tell me which permissions the account we would connect as actually has.

Where we are: nothing is connected, and nothing has been written to your Jira. The permission set above is wider than I am comfortable handing to software that acts on its own, so we are putting a limit on our side before we connect. Until that is done we will not write to your Jira at all. Whatever we settle on, the only thing our bots will be able to do is add a note to tickets you name, and we will agree that list with you in writing first.

You can revoke the connection from your side at any time, without telling us.

If any of this is wrong for your setup, tell me and we will stop.
```

## What each choice does

**Accept — you send it now.** DataTap learns the width before it grants access. No write goes to their Jira. The message stays correct for every CTO answer. Nothing is committed to DataTap.

**Reject — you hold it.** Then do not approve the Jira access card. The message waits for the CTO answer on 7 October 2026.

## Why I recommend accept

The message commits us to nothing. It asks DataTap for two things and promises no write. Waiting buys no accuracy. It buys one risk: a surprise on a client production site.

> - Your **people records** — position, manager and talent records — and who is allocated to what.
> - Your **source code**, through code search.

>

> wider than I am comfortable handing to software that acts on its own, so **we will not write to your
> Jira at all until we have put a limit on our side and you have agreed to it.** When that limit is in
> place, the only thing our bots will be able to do is add a note to tickets you name, and we will agree
> that list with you in writing first.
>

**What changed from what you would have sent an hour ago.**

- **Two promises made ours, and one of them was not safe.** The old text said the only thing our bots *will be able to* do is add a comment. The text now commits to behaviour only: we will not write to their Jira **at all** until we have a limit and they have agreed to it. That is true on every path, including the one where we connect without the brake, and it means we never write in that case.
- **The disclosure was incomplete.** Our own Security review found four surfaces missing from it: Confluence can change *who has permission* on a page (bigger than the public-link point we had), Loom videos can be made public, teams can be created with open membership, and the grant reaches code search and HR-style records.
